Q60-C.text:
# Rehearsal Plan: 5 Rehearsals to December 20

## Before Rehearsal 1: Three Quick Decisions

Spend 10 minutes on these first. They shape everything else.

**1. Rank the new songs by difficulty.** The plan calls them **N1** (hardest), **N2** and **N3** (easiest). The hardest song gets the most time, and it always comes early in the rehearsal while voices and brains are fresh.

**2. Rank the known songs by how much work they need.** These are **P1** (most work) through **P4** (nearly ready). If you're unsure, ask your section leaders which spots feel shaky.

**3. Mark which songs are piano-heavy.** This is the biggest risk in your schedule. If a new song is piano-heavy, you can't wait until rehearsal 4 to start it. Two rehearsals isn't enough to learn notes *and* fit them to the piano. Instead:

- **Rehearsals 1–3:** Learn the vocal parts using your own keyboard, part recordings or a practice track.
- **Rehearsals 4–5:** Put the voices and piano together: tempo, intros, entrances, balance and interludes.

**Strongly recommended:** contact your accompanist this week.
- Ask them to **record the piano parts**, even on a phone. Having them by rehearsal 2 or 3 lets the choir practise entrances against the real accompaniment. This one step will save you the most time in rehearsal 4.
- Agree on **tempos, intro lengths, repeats and cuts** in advance so rehearsal 4 isn't spent negotiating.
- Ask which passages *they* expect to be hardest to coordinate, and plan to start with those.

## The Overall Shape

| Rehearsal | Theme | Goal by the end |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | Learn | All 3 new songs introduced. The hardest sections have been tackled. |
| **2** | Consolidate | New songs learned all the way through. Known songs diagnosed. |
| **3** | Secure *(last without piano)* | New songs sung start to finish with confident notes. Polish well under way. **Decision point.** |
| **4** | Integrate *(piano)* | Piano pieces fitted together. Everything rehearsed in its concert form. |
| **5** | Perform *(piano)* | Full run in concert order. Fine-tuning only, no note-learning. |

About 450 minutes in total. Roughly 55% goes to the new songs in rehearsals 1–3. The last two rehearsals are about putting the concert together.

## Rehearsal 1: Learn

| Time | Activity | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 0:00–0:10 | **Warm-up** | Build it around the new songs' challenges: a tricky interval, a rhythm pattern, a vowel. |
| 0:10–0:38 | **N1** (28 min) | Play or sing through once so everyone hears the whole song. Then start on the **hardest section**, not bar 1. |
| 0:38–1:00 | **N2** (22 min) | Same approach. Aim to cover at least half the song. |
| 1:00–1:03 | Stretch / water | Short and standing. Keeps focus up. |
| 1:03–1:18 | **N3** (15 min) | The easiest song comes when energy dips. You might get most of the way through it. |
| 1:18–1:28 | **P1 and P2: diagnosis** (10 min) | Sing straight through without stopping. You and the section leaders note the problem spots. Don't fix yet. |
| 1:28–1:30 | Wrap-up | Point to practice tracks. Give a specific "homework" passage. |

**Note-learning tips:**
- Speak tricky rhythms before singing them.
- Learn hard passages on "loo" before adding text.
- Teach one part at a time while the others hum quietly, so no one sits idle.
- If you have section leaders, a 10-minute split into sectionals inside the N1 block can double your efficiency.

## Rehearsal 2: Consolidate

| Time | Activity | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 0:00–0:10 | **Warm-up** | Include a passage from N1 *inside* the warm-up as a memory check. |
| 0:10–0:35 | **N1** (25 min) | Review last week's sections (expect some forgetting, that's normal). Then learn the rest. |
| 0:35–0:55 | **N2** (20 min) | Finish learning. Join the sections together. |
| 0:55–0:58 | Stretch / water | |
| 0:58–1:10 | **N3** (12 min) | Finish learning. Attempt a full sing-through. |
| 1:10–1:28 | **Polish** (18 min) | Diagnose P3 and P4 with a straight sing-through (~8 min). Then spend ~10 min fixing the **worst spots** found in P1 and P2 last week. |
| 1:28–1:30 | Wrap-up | Homework: listen to the new songs with the score. |

## Rehearsal 3: Secure (last rehearsal without piano)

| Time | Activity | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 0:00–0:10 | **Warm-up** | |
| 0:10–0:30 | **N1** (20 min) | Fix weak spots, then sing it **start to finish**. If you have the piano recording, practise the entrances against it. |
| 0:30–0:45 | **N2** (15 min) | Same: fix, then a full run. |
| 0:45–0:57 | **N3** (12 min) | Same. |
| 0:57–1:00 | Stretch / water | |
| 1:00–1:25 | **Polish P1–P4** (25 min) | Spend the time by need, for example P1 10 min, P2 7, P3 5, P4 3. Work on dynamics, consonants, phrase endings and confident openings, not just notes. |
| 1:25–1:30 | **Decision point** and wrap-up | See below. |

**Checkpoint:** by the end of rehearsal 3, every new song should get through from start to finish with mostly secure notes.

**If a new song isn't there**, decide now, not in rehearsal 5. Your options:
- **Simplify it:** sing it in unison or two parts, cut a verse, or give a hard passage to a small group or soloist.
- **Drop it** and give its time to the other six songs.

A confident six-song concert beats a shaky seven-song one. Deciding now leaves rehearsals 4 and 5 for the music you'll actually perform.

## Rehearsal 4: Integrate (accompanist present)

The accompanist's time is your scarcest resource, so the piano pieces come first.

| Time | Activity | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 0:00–0:10 | **Warm-up** | Have the accompanist play it. This settles everyone into working together. |
| 0:10–0:55 | **Piano-heavy pieces** (45 min) | **New piano songs first** (~20 min each), then known piano songs (~5–10 min each). Order of work below. |
| 0:55–0:58 | Break | |
| 0:58–1:20 | **Other pieces** (22 min) | Lightly accompanied and a cappella songs. If the accompanist isn't needed, you could let them leave early or ask them to arrive later. Agree this in advance. |
| 1:20–1:30 | **Partial run in concert order** (10 min) | Run 2–3 songs back to back *with the transitions*: pitch-giving, page turns, pauses. |

**Order of work for each piano piece:**
1. **Intro and first entrance.** Can the choir find their note and come in together after the piano intro? Mark the cue in everyone's score.
2. **Tempo agreement.** Choirs often rush or drag compared with how they rehearsed alone.
3. **Interludes and re-entrances.** Choirs most often get lost here, so count them out loud the first time.
4. **Balance.** Is the piano covering the voices anywhere? Should the choir sing out more?
5. **The ending.** Final chord, cut-off and how long the piano holds after it.

Record this rehearsal on a phone. Listening back for 10 minutes afterwards will show you exactly what to fix in rehearsal 5.

## Rehearsal 5: Perform (accompanist present)

**No new note-learning.** This rehearsal is about confidence and flow, and about protecting voices.

| Time | Activity | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 0:00–0:08 | **Warm-up** | Use the same warm-up you'll do on concert day so it becomes routine. |
| 0:08–0:20 | **Fixes from rehearsal 4** (12 min) | Only the problems you noted from the recording. Piano pieces first. |
| 0:20–0:25 | **Stage logistics** (5 min) | Walking on and off, standing order, folders up and down, bows, where to look. |
| 0:25–1:05 | **Full run in concert order** (40 min) | **Don't stop**, whatever happens. Include spoken introductions and transitions. Note problems silently. |
| 1:05–1:08 | Break | |
| 1:08–1:25 | **Targeted fixes** (17 min) | Openings, endings and piano handoffs. These are what the audience notices most. |
| 1:25–1:30 | **Finish strong** | Sing the opening song one last time. Go over concert-day logistics (call time, dress, water) and send them home feeling good. |

If you can hold rehearsal 5 **in the concert venue**, do it. The acoustics, the piano and the standing positions will all feel different, and it's much better to find that out at a rehearsal.

## Between Rehearsals

- **Practice tracks:** send part recordings for the new songs after rehearsal 1, plus the accompanist's piano recording once you have it.
- **Specific homework:** "Altos, bars 24–40 of N1" works far better than "please practise."
- **Section leaders:** a 2-minute message to their section mid-week keeps momentum going.
- **Spacing:** with weekly rehearsals, avoid putting rehearsal 5 the night before the concert if you can. Two or three days before gives voices time to rest.

## Concert-Day Tips

- Keep the warm-up short (10–15 min). Briefly run the start of each song and any tricky piano entrances. Don't sing everything at full voice.
- December is cold and flu season, so remind everyone to rest their voices and drink water during the week before.
- Put a printed running order in every folder and on the piano.

If you send me the song titles and say which are piano-heavy, I can fill in this template with exact minutes for each song and suggest a concert running order that balances energy and gives voices a rest.

Q18-A2.text:
# Saturday Tournament Rotation

## The Numbers

- 4 matches × 30 minutes = **120 minutes** of football
- 7 players on the pitch = **840 player-minutes** to share
- Someone must be in goal for all 120 minutes, and only Tunde and Chidi can do it, so they cover **60 minutes each**.
- The other 16 players share 6 outfield spots × 120 minutes = 720 minutes, which is **exactly 45 minutes each**.

So every outfield player plays **3 full halves**, and **you only make changes at half-time**. Tunde and Chidi get 60 minutes each, which is as close to equal as their role allows.

## Setup

Put your 16 outfield players into **8 pairs (A–H)**. Pairs always come on together, so it helps to pair a defensive player with an attacking one. That way each half has a balanced team.

| Pair | Players |
|---|---|
| A | ______ & ______ |
| B | ______ & ______ |
| C | ______ & ______ |
| D | ______ & ______ |
| E | ______ & ______ |
| F | ______ & ______ |
| G | ______ & ______ |
| H | ______ & ______ |

## Rotation

| Half | Goalkeeper | Outfield (6) | Resting |
|---|---|---|---|
| Match 1, 1st half | Tunde | A, D, F | B, C, E, G, H + Chidi |
| Match 1, 2nd half | Chidi | B, E, G | A, C, D, F, H + Tunde |
| Match 2, 1st half | Tunde | C, F, H | A, B, D, E, G + Chidi |
| Match 2, 2nd half | Chidi | A, D, G | B, C, E, F, H + Tunde |
| Match 3, 1st half | Tunde | B, E, H | A, C, D, F, G + Chidi |
| Match 3, 2nd half | Chidi | A, C, F | B, D, E, G, H + Tunde |
| Match 4, 1st half | Tunde | B, D, G | A, C, E, F, H + Chidi |
| Match 4, 2nd half | Chidi | C, E, H | A, B, D, F, G + Tunde |

## Each Player's Halves

| Pair | Plays | Sits out |
|---|---|---|
| A | M1 1st, M2 2nd, M3 2nd | Match 4 |
| B | M1 2nd, M3 1st, M4 1st | Match 2 |
| C | M2 1st, M3 2nd, M4 2nd | Match 1 |
| D | M1 1st, M2 2nd, M4 1st | Match 3 |
| E | M1 2nd, M3 1st, M4 2nd | Match 2 |
| F | M1 1st, M2 1st, M3 2nd | Match 4 |
| G | M1 2nd, M2 2nd, M4 1st | Match 3 |
| H | M2 1st, M3 1st, M4 2nd | Match 1 |

**Result:** every outfield player gets 45 minutes, plays in 3 of the 4 matches, and never plays more than 2 halves in a row. Tunde and Chidi each get 60 minutes in goal.

## Tips

- **Print the rotation table** and give it to a parent helper so half-time changes are quick.
- **If a keeper gets injured or tired,** the other can cover the remaining halves. Just know that their minutes will go up.
- **If you want Tunde and Chidi to play outfield too,** they can swap into a pair for a half while resting from goal. This gives them more total minutes, but some kids enjoy the variety.
- **If someone doesn't show up,** their partner still plays the same halves. You'll have one spare slot in those 3 halves, so give it to whoever is next in line.

Q12-A2.text:
# Half Marathon Plan: 16 Weeks, Thursday to Sunday

**Check your race day first.** March 8, 2027 is a **Monday**, which is a night-shift day for you. If that's right, try to get that Monday night off now. Running 21 km in the morning and then working a 12-hour night shift is hard on your body and risky at work. The plan below already treats Saturday and Sunday as race prep, with no long run that weekend.

## How each week works

| Day | What | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Thu** | Rest | You're coming off three night shifts. Sleep matters more than miles. Light walking or stretching in the evening is fine. |
| **Fri** | Key run (easy, strides, tempo or race pace) | You're rested by Friday, so this is your best day for harder efforts. |
| **Sat** | Short easy run | Very relaxed. Skip it if you're tired. |
| **Sun** | Long run | It's followed by four days off running, so you get plenty of recovery. |

**Easy** means you can talk in full sentences. **Tempo** means comfortably hard, where you can only speak a few words at a time. **Strides** are 4–6 relaxed 20-second pickups after an easy run.

## The schedule (km)

| Wk | Dates | Fri | Sat | Sun (long) | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Nov 19–22 | 5 easy | 4 easy | 8 | 17 |
| 2 | Nov 26–29 | 5 easy + strides | 5 easy | 9 | 19 |
| 3 | Dec 3–6 | 6 easy + strides | 5 easy | 10 | 21 |
| 4 | Dec 10–13 *(easier week)* | 5 easy | 4 easy | 8 | 17 |
| 5 | Dec 17–20 | 6 incl. 3×5 min tempo | 5 easy | 11 | 22 |
| 6 | Dec 24–27 | 6 incl. 3×5 min tempo | 5 easy | 12 | 23 |
| 7 | Dec 31–Jan 3 | 7 incl. 15 min tempo | 5 easy | 13 | 25 |
| 8 | Jan 7–10 *(easier week)* | 5 easy + strides | 5 easy | 10 | 20 |
| 9 | Jan 14–17 | 7 incl. 2×10 min tempo | 6 easy | 14 | 27 |
| 10 | Jan 21–24 | 8 incl. 20 min tempo | 6 easy | 15 | 29 |
| 11 | Jan 28–31 | 8 incl. 5×3 min hard / 2 min jog | 6 easy | 16 | 30 |
| 12 | Feb 4–7 *(easier week)* | 6 easy + strides | 5 easy | 12 | 23 |
| 13 | Feb 11–14 | 8 incl. 25 min tempo | 6 easy | 18 | 32 |
| 14 | Feb 18–21 | 9 incl. 3×2 km at race pace | 6 easy | 19 (last 3 km at race pace) | 34 |
| 15 | Feb 25–28 *(taper)* | 7 incl. 3 km at race pace | 5 easy | 13 | 25 |
| 16 | Mar 4–7 *(race week)* | 5 easy + strides | 3 shakeout or rest | Rest | **Race Mon 8** |

The easier weeks (4, 8, 12) are on purpose. They let your body absorb the training, so don't skip them.

## Beating the heat

- **Finish long runs by 7am.** By weeks 13–14 your long run may take over 2 hours, so you'll need to start around 4:30–4:45. A lit route or a headlamp helps.
- **Evenings are fine for Friday and Saturday runs,** ideally after sunset.
- **Run by effort, not pace.** Heat makes everything feel harder, and slowing down is normal.
- **Bring water and electrolytes** on any run over an hour.
- **Practice race fueling from week 9.** Take a gel or snack about every 40–45 minutes on long runs, using what you plan to use on race day.
- **Practice your race morning.** Find out the start time and rehearse your wake-up, breakfast and timing on a couple of long runs.

## Night-shift tips

- **Protect your sleep.** If you slept badly, make Friday an easy run instead of a workout.
- **Add some strength work.** 15–20 minutes of squats, lunges, calf raises and planks once or twice a week helps a lot. It can go on Thursday evening or before a Monday shift if you feel up to it.
- **Expect week 1 to be a bigger jump** if you're currently running less than about 15 km a week. If it feels too much, repeat week 1 before moving on. There's no room for extra weeks, so stay flexible, but don't push through pain.

Want me to adjust anything, like moving the long run to Saturday or aiming for a target finish time?

Q58-C.text:
# Hanoi → Laos → Cambodia → Bangkok: 54-Day Route and Budget (USD 2,800)

## The short answer

- **Daily limit: about $33/day in Laos and Cambodia, and $45/day in Thailand.** This covers your bed, food, drinks, local transport and small entry fees.
- **The big costs are budgeted separately.** Visas, long-distance buses and trains, the Angkor pass and the Thakhek Loop bike come to about $570 in total.
- **Keep $300 as an untouchable reserve.** It covers missed buses, a doctor visit, a lost phone, or a taxi to the airport if everything goes wrong.

Today is 17 Nov and your flight is 10 Jan, which gives you **54 nights**. That's closer to 7½ weeks than 7, so you have a few extra days.

---

## 1. Budget math

| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| Starting cash | **$2,800** |
| Emergency reserve (don't touch) | –$300 |
| Visas (Laos ~$45, Cambodia ~$36, Thailand $0 for most passports) | –$81 |
| Long-distance transport (18 legs, itemised below) | –$205 |
| Angkor 3-day pass ($62) plus tuk-tuk for 3 days (~$60) | –$120 |
| Thakhek Loop motorbike (4 days plus fuel) | –$60 |
| Activities fund (Kuang Si, Erawan, Ayutthaya, kayaking etc.) | –$100 |
| **Left for daily spending** | **$1,934** |

How the daily money is split:

| Country | Nights | Per day | Total |
|---|---|---|---|
| Vietnam (remaining) | 3 | $30 | $90 |
| Laos | 27 | $33 | $891 |
| Cambodia | 13 | $33 | $429 |
| Thailand | 11 | $45 | $495 |
| **Total** | **54** | | **$1,905** |

That leaves about $30 of slack on top of the $300 reserve. Thailand gets a higher limit because Bangkok over New Year is the most expensive part of the trip.

**What $33/day looks like in Laos or Cambodia:**
- Dorm bed $7–10, or a basic private guesthouse room $12–18 (good value if you're two people)
- Food $12–15, mostly street food or local restaurants at $2–4 a meal
- Local transport (tuk-tuks, bicycle hire) $3–5
- Beer, coffee and snacks $4–6

Luang Prabang and Vang Vieng tend to run over this. Pakse, Thakhek and Kratie tend to run under, so they balance out.

---

## 2. The route, day by day

### Vietnam (3 nights)

| Dates | Where | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 17–18 Nov | **Hanoi** | Prep day: get USD cash for visas, check your Vietnam visa expiry, buy a sleeper bus ticket. |
| 18 Nov (night) | Sleeper bus to **Dien Bien Phu** | About 10–11 hours, ~$20. |
| 19 Nov | **Dien Bien Phu** | Rest, and visit the battlefield museum. Buy your bus ticket to Muang Khua at the bus station. |

### Laos (27 nights, 20 Nov to 17 Dec)

| Dates | Where | Nights | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 20 Nov | → **Muang Khua** | 1 | Bus leaves around 5:30–6:00 am, ~$12, about 8 hours. You cross at the Tay Trang / Sop Hun border. |
| 21–24 Nov | **Nong Khiaw** (+ Muang Ngoi) | 4 | The road from Muang Khua is ~$8; the Nam Ou boats mostly no longer run because of dams. Take the 1-hour boat to Muang Ngoi for 1–2 nights, and hike to the viewpoints. |
| 25–29 Nov | **Luang Prabang** | 5 | Minivan ~$10. See Kuang Si Falls, the night market and the morning alms. This is the priciest town, so eat at the night market buffet. |
| 30 Nov–2 Dec | **Vang Vieng** | 3 | Laos–China Railway, ~$15–20. Visit the lagoons and caves, rent a bicycle. |
| 3–4 Dec | **Vientiane** | 2 | Train ~$10–12. Visit COPE and Buddha Park. |
| 5–9 Dec | **Thakhek** (Loop) | 5 | Bus ~$10. Do the 3–4 day motorbike loop through Kong Lor Cave, a highlight of the trip. |
| 10–11 Dec | **Pakse** | 2 | Bus ~$8. Optional Bolaven Plateau coffee and waterfalls day trip. |
| 12–16 Dec | **4000 Islands** (Don Det / Don Khon) | 5 | Minivan plus boat ~$10. Cycling, Mekong sunsets, Khone Phapheng falls. Very cheap; a good place to bank savings. |

**Your Laos visa is about 30 days.** You'd be in the country for 28, so there's little slack. If you lose time early on, cut nights from Don Det rather than overstaying (fines are about $10/day).

### Cambodia (13 nights, 17–30 Dec)

| Dates | Where | Nights | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 17–18 Dec | → **Kratie** | 2 | Through-minibus from Don Det, ~$20, 6–8 hours. See the Irrawaddy dolphins and cycle on Koh Trong island. |
| 19–21 Dec | **Phnom Penh** | 3 | Bus ~$10. Visit Tuol Sleng (S-21) and the Killing Fields. |
| 22–25 Dec | **Kampot** (+ Kep day trip) | 4 | Bus ~$10. A cheap, relaxed spot for Christmas: river, pepper farms, Kep crab market. |
| 26–29 Dec | **Siem Reap** | 4 | Direct bus ~$15, or go via Phnom Penh. Use the Angkor 3-day pass on 3 of your 4 days. |

### Thailand (11 nights, 30 Dec to 10 Jan)

| Dates | Where | Nights | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 30 Dec | → **Bangkok** | 3 | Cross at Poipet / Aranyaprathet, ~$20 by through-bus. Spend New Year's Eve in Bangkok. **Book this accommodation now.** |
| 2–5 Jan | **Kanchanaburi** | 4 | Train or minivan ~$4. Visit Erawan Falls and the Death Railway. Cheaper than Bangkok, so it helps the Thai budget. |
| 6–7 Jan | **Ayutthaya** | 2 | Minivan ~$8, or go back through Bangkok. Rent a bicycle to see the temple ruins. |
| 8–9 Jan | **Bangkok**, near your airport | 2 | Train ~$3. |
| **10 Jan** | **Flight home** | | |

**Why cross on 30 Dec:** the Poipet border and buses get very crowded around New Year, and you avoid travelling on 31 Dec or 1 Jan.

---

## 3. Money checkpoints

These figures already account for the big one-off costs, so you only need to compare them with your actual balance.

| Date | Where | You should have at least |
|---|---|---|
| 20 Nov | Entering Laos | **$2,630** |
| 5 Dec | Arriving in Thakhek | **$2,050** |
| 17 Dec | Leaving Laos | **$1,560** |
| 30 Dec | Leaving Cambodia | **$890** |
| 10 Jan | Flight day | **$300** (the untouched reserve) |

**Recalculate your daily limit each Sunday with this formula:**

> (money left − $300 reserve − big costs still ahead) ÷ nights left

If the result is above your limit, you can loosen up a bit. If it's below, use the cuts listed below. A simple way to stick to it is to take your daily limit out in cash each morning and keep the rest separate.

---

## 4. If you fall behind, or get ahead

**If you're behind, cut in this order:**
1. Use dorms everywhere, including Bangkok.
2. Do the short Thakhek Loop (2–3 days) or join a group to share costs.
3. Skip Ayutthaya and spend those 2 nights in Kanchanaburi, which saves ~$15.
4. Cut beer. It's often $3–5 a day without you noticing.

**If you're ahead,** good uses for the extra are:
- 2 nights on Koh Rong Samloem from Kampot (~$60–80 extra)
- A cooking class in Luang Prabang
- A private room around Christmas or New Year

---

## 5. Things to check before you leave Hanoi

These depend on your passport or may have changed, so please confirm them:

1. **Vietnam visa expiry.** Make sure your visa covers you until 20 Nov.
2. **Laos visa.**
   - Visa on arrival at Sop Hun costs about $30–45 depending on nationality, plus about $1–2 in "fees". You need a passport photo and **clean, new USD notes**.
   - Check that this border issues visas on arrival for your nationality. If it doesn't, get an e-visa in advance.
3. **Cambodia visa.**
   - The e-visa costs about $36 and is worth it. The Laos–Cambodia land border is known for asking $2–5 in unofficial "stamp fees", and the e-visa avoids most of this.
   - Cambodia also has an online e-Arrival form. Check whether you need to fill it in.
4. **Thailand entry.**
   - The visa-free stay length has been changing. You only need 11 days, but check the current rules for your passport.
   - Fill in the **Thailand Digital Arrival Card (TDAC)** online within 3 days before you cross.
5. **Your airport and departure time.** Check whether you fly from Suvarnabhumi (BKK) or Don Mueang (DMK). If your flight is early, stay near that airport on 9 Jan.
6. **Travel insurance.** If you don't have it, it's the most important thing to sort out. The $300 reserve won't cover a motorbike accident on the Loop. Wear a helmet, and check whether your policy covers motorbikes.

---

## 6. Practical tips that protect the budget

- **Laos–China Railway:** buy tickets 3–7 days ahead with the LCR Ticket app or at stations. December is peak season and trains sell out. If you can't get a seat, the minivan is the backup.
- **Cash:**
  - Laos ATMs: each withdrawal costs about $1–3 and is capped at a low amount (roughly $50–100). Take out the maximum each time.
  - Cambodia: you'll mostly pay in USD, and ATMs charge $4–5 per withdrawal, so take out large amounts.
  - Thailand: ATMs charge about 220 baht (~$6) per withdrawal, so make one large withdrawal.
  - Always choose to be charged in the local currency when a card machine or ATM offers a choice; the "pay in your home currency" option has a worse rate.
  - A Wise or Revolut card helps with all of this.
- **Bring $100–150 in clean USD notes** for visas and the Laos–Cambodia border. Torn or old notes are often refused.
- **Pack warm clothes:** Dien Bien Phu, Nong Khiaw and the Loop drop to 8–12°C on December mornings. Bring a fleece and a buff.
- **Book Bangkok for 30 Dec to 2 Jan now.** Prices around New Year can double, and the cheap beds go first.
- **Watch out for these traps:**
  - Shared bus tickets sold through your guesthouse that come with a hidden "border fee"
  - Fake visa offices before the border at Poipet; only pay at the official building
  - Taxis at Poipet; use the official bus or shared taxi instead

---

**About these prices:** they're typical backpacker prices as far as I know, so treat them as estimates. The Lao kip in particular keeps losing value, so check local prices when you arrive. The route works because the plan is padded with the activities fund and the $300 reserve.

If you'd like, I can turn this into a spreadsheet that recalculates your daily limit as you log what you spend, or rework the route. For example, I could cut the Thakhek Loop to add Koh Rong, or take a faster route if you'd rather skip northern Laos.

Q16-A2.text:
# 12-Day Portugal Itinerary: Lisbon, the Algarve and Porto (Knee-Friendly)

**The short version:** $6,000 is enough for a comfortable trip if you book flights early. The route below uses three bases so you only change hotels twice. Each day pairs one main outing with plenty of sitting: boats, trams, scenic rides and long lunches.

**Route:** Lisbon (4 nights) → Tavira, Algarve (3 nights) → Porto (4 nights), then fly home from Porto.

**One suggestion:** book an "open-jaw" ticket, flying into Lisbon and home from Porto. It usually costs about the same as a round trip and saves a 3-hour backtrack. If you'd rather fly home from Lisbon, take the train back on Day 12 morning and fly that afternoon or the next day.

**About hills:** Lisbon and Porto are both very hilly, with slippery cobblestones. The plan avoids climbs by using taxis, tuk-tuks, a cable car and boats. Bolt and Uber are cheap here, usually €5–10 per ride.

---

## Day-by-Day

**Day 0 – Depart Columbus.** There are no nonstop flights, so expect one connection, typically Newark, JFK, Boston, Toronto or Philadelphia. Most flights are overnight and land in the morning.

### Lisbon (4 nights)
Stay in **Baixa or lower Chiado**, the flattest central area. Request a room with an elevator.

- **Day 1 – Arrive, take it easy.** Taxi or Uber from the airport (~€15–20). Stroll the flat Baixa grid to Praça do Comércio and sit by the river. Early dinner.
- **Day 2 – Belém (almost entirely flat).** Take Tram 15, a modern car with easy boarding. See Jerónimos Monastery and Belém Tower, have custard tarts at Pastéis de Belém, and walk the riverfront. In the evening, visit Time Out Market, which has lots of seating.
- **Day 3 – Alfama the easy way.** Hire a tuk-tuk tour (~€60–90 for 1–1.5 hrs) to the hilltop viewpoints and São Jorge Castle, then walk only the downhill stretches. Have a slow lunch, rest in the afternoon, and book a **fado dinner** in the evening.
- **Day 4 – Sintra day trip.** A small-group tour or a private driver saves the most walking. At Pena Palace, pay for the **park shuttle** from the gate to the palace, because the walk up is steep. Skip Quinta da Regaleira's spiral well, which is all stairs. For a gentler alternative, spend a half-day in **Cascais**, a seaside town with a flat promenade.

### Tavira, Algarve (3 nights)
Tavira is a flat, pretty riverside town, unlike Lagos, which is built around cliffs.

- **Day 5 – Train to the Algarve.** Lisbon to Faro takes about 3 hours, then a short regional train or taxi to Tavira. Evening by the river.
- **Day 6 – Beach day.** Go to **Praia do Barril**, where a little tourist train runs across the lagoon so you don't have to walk 1 km on sand. Rent chairs and an umbrella and have a seafood lunch.
- **Day 7 – Ria Formosa boat tour.** This is a lagoon and island-hopping trip from Olhão or Faro, mostly sitting. Alternatively, do nothing at all.

### Porto (4 nights)
Stay near **São Bento or Aliados** for metro access. Avoid lodging that sits partway up the riverside hills.

- **Day 8 – Fly Faro → Porto (~1 hr).** Settle in, then have dinner at the riverfront in Ribeira. Take a taxi down and back up.
- **Day 9 – Riverside Porto.** Do the **Six Bridges cruise** (50 min, seated) and port-wine cellar tastings in Gaia, which are flat along the river. Ride the **Gaia cable car** up and the **Guindais funicular** to skip the steepest climbs.
- **Day 10 – Douro Valley tour.** Choose a full-day van tour with a river boat ride, wine tastings and lunch. It's a highlight of the trip and involves very little walking.
- **Day 11 – Aveiro day trip.** About 1 hour by train. Aveiro is flat, with canals and painted *moliceiro* boats. Back for a farewell dinner. In Porto, skip Clérigos Tower, which has 240 steps.

**Day 12 – Fly home from Porto.**

---

## Rough Cost Breakdown (for two, USD)

| Category | Estimate | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Flights CMH ↔ Portugal | $2,000 | ~$1,000/person economy. Book by Jan–Feb, since May fills up. |
| Faro → Porto flight | $160 | Includes a checked bag. |
| Lodging (11 nights) | $1,550 | Lisbon ~$160/night, Tavira ~$120, Porto ~$135. Includes small city tourist taxes. |
| Food | $1,100 | ~$90/day. Lunch specials (*prato do dia*) run €10–15/person with wine. |
| Local transport | $400 | Trains, airport transfers, frequent Bolt/Uber rides to spare the knee. |
| Activities & tours | $650 | Sintra tour/tickets, Jerónimos, fado dinner, tuk-tuk, Ria Formosa, river cruise, port tastings, Douro tour (~$250). |
| **Total** | **~$5,860** | Leaves ~$140 buffer. |

**If it runs over:**
- **Flights above $1,100/person:** drop the Algarve and do 6 nights Lisbon, 5 nights Porto. That saves the internal flight and one hotel change, about $300–400.
- **Lodging:** guesthouses (*alojamento local*) are often cheaper than hotels. Always confirm there's an elevator.
- **Travel insurance:** consider it, about $150–250 for two. It isn't included above.

## Knee Tips

- **Shoes:** wear grippy soles. Portuguese cobblestones (*calçada*) are slick, especially when wet.
- **Lodging:** ask every hotel about **elevators and steps to the entrance** before booking. Many old buildings have neither.
- **Daily pace:** plan one main outing per day with an afternoon rest. Portugal's late dinner culture (8pm or later) makes that easy.
- **Getting around:** use rides freely. A €7 Bolt ride up a hill is the best money you'll spend.

These prices are estimates, so check current fares when you book. I'd be glad to adjust the plan, for example with fewer hotel changes, more beach time, or a version that flies home from Lisbon.
